# Fast sum of two two-limb numbers

<!-- Generated by docs/tools/reference.py from gen/claims.json, gen/kernels/, include/kairn/gen/bounds.hpp, proofs/gen/Statements.v, results/milestone1/brute/ and docs/tools/reference_operations.py. Do not edit: run python3 docs/tools/reference.py. -->

Kernel `add_fast_2_2` · proved · [all operations](index.md) · [how to read this page](reading.md)

## What it computes

An approximation $z$ of $x + y$:

$$z \approx x + y.$$

A number of several limbs stands for their exact sum: $x = x_0 + x_1$, $y = y_0 + y_1$, $z = z_0 + z_1$.

## C++

| Form | Operands | Result | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| `add_fast(x, y)` | `Expansion<T, 2>`, `Expansion<T, 2>` | `Expansion<T, 2>` |  |

`T` is `float` or `double`; the operations are in namespace `kairn`, header `kairn/kairn.hpp`. The operators and functions also accept the marker `kairn::unverified` on an operand, which they need while the kernel is UNVERIFIED.

## Requires

- Every limb of every operand is a finite number of `T`.
- $x$ is normalized: $x_0 = \mathrm{RN}(x_0 + x_1)$.
- $y$ is normalized: $y_0 = \mathrm{RN}(y_0 + y_1)$.

## Guarantees

When the requirements hold and no operation of the kernel overflows:

- $z$ is normalized: $z_0 = \mathrm{RN}(z_0 + z_1)$.
- $\lvert z - (x + y)\rvert \le 3\,u^2\,(\lvert x\rvert + \lvert y\rvert)$.

The constants of the bound, for each limb type, from `gen/claims.json`; `kairn::traits` exports them rounded up to `T`:

| | `double` | `float` |
|---|---|---|
| unit roundoff $u$ | $2^{-53}$ | $2^{-24}$ |
| relative term $c\,u^2$ | $3 \cdot 2^{-106} \approx 3.6978 \times 10^{-32}$ | $3 \cdot 2^{-48} \approx 1.0658 \times 10^{-14}$ |
| `unit`, `tiny`, as compiled | `0x1.8p-105`, `0.0` | `0x1.8p-47f`, `0.0f` |

The compiled constants are the entry `add_fast` of `kairn::traits<Expansion<T, 2>>`: `unit` and `tiny` bound the error relative to the sum of the magnitudes of the operands (`reference` is `BoundForm::operands`); no bound relative to the computed value follows, and `unit_computed` and `tiny_computed` are $+\infty$.

Proved for every binary format with a precision of at least 2 bits and any exponent range, rounding to nearest with ties to even and with gradual underflow, in the model where no operation overflows. Both limb types qualify: `double` has 53 bits, `float` has 24 bits.

## Status

**Proved.** Rocq checks the theorem `add_fast_2_2_correct`, in [`proofs/theories/AddFast22.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/theories/AddFast22.v), against `add_fast_2_2_spec`, the statement the generator prints from these claims into [`proofs/gen/Statements.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/gen/Statements.v); `make -C proofs` finds no axiom in its proof beyond the four allowed ([Proofs](../proofs/index.md)).

The statement, as Rocq reads it (the vocabulary, `fmt`, `RN`, `u`, `eta` and `normalized_2`, is defined at the top of the same file; `emin` is the exponent of $\eta$ and `prec` the precision):

```coq
Definition add_fast_2_2_spec : Prop :=
  forall emin prec : Z, (2 <= prec)%Z ->
  forall x0 x1 y0 y1 : R,
  normalized_2 emin prec x0 x1 ->
  normalized_2 emin prec y0 y1 ->
  let '(z0, z1) := add_fast_2_2 emin prec tie_even x0 x1 y0 y1 in
  normalized_2 emin prec z0 z1 /\
  Rabs ((z0 + z1) - ((x0 + x1) + (y0 + y1))) <= 3 * u prec ^ 2 * (Rabs (x0 + x1) + Rabs (y0 + y1)).
```

## Source

**Algorithm:** [JMP17](../developer/design/phase0/references.md#jmp17) Alg. 5 (SloppyDWPlusDW); the bound and the normalization are proved here. **License:** algorithm: published; proof: MIT.

## Listing

From [`gen/kernels/add_fast_2_2.kernel`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/gen/kernels/add_fast_2_2.kernel), the description the C++ and the formal model are generated from. Each line is one operation of `T`, rounded to nearest; `prod(a, b)` is $\mathrm{RN}(ab)$, written as a fused multiply-add with a zero addend ([the kernel IR](../developer/architecture.md#the-kernel-ir)).
It calls [`two_sum`](two_sum.md), [`fast_two_sum`](fast_two_sum.md).

```
# SloppyDWPlusDW, ending with Fast2Sum. The result is normalized even when the leading limbs
# cancel, and the error is at most 3 u^2 (|x| + |y|), with no underflow term: both are proved
# (proofs/theories/AddFast22.v). The bound is relative to |x| + |y|, not to |x + y|.

(sh, sl) = two_sum(x0, y0)
v        = add(x1, y1)
w        = add(sl, v)
(z0, z1) = fast_two_sum(sh, w)
```

## Measured

The latest brute-force runs, from the stored summaries in [`results/milestone1/brute/`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/tree/main/results/milestone1/brute) ([the report](../developer/results/brute-milestone1.md#add_fast_2_2)): the oracle judged, in exact arithmetic, the results of the compiled kernel (every compiler, scalar and packed code, every contraction setting) on random operands of `binary64` and `binary32`, and those of the generator's interpreter on every operand of small formats. A measurement, not a bound.

| Run | Cases judged | Failed | largest error / bound | Bound attained |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `binary64` (`double`), compiled: 40 runners on 3 machines | 64 298 616 | 0 | 0.766145 | no |
| `binary32` (`float`), compiled: 40 runners on 3 machines | 64 285 512 | 0 | 0.502673 | no |
| toy formats, every operand: 6 domains of 6 formats | 15 001 304 | 0 | 0.671916 (`fp:4:-4:3`) | no |

## Not claimed

- Anything when an operand is infinite or NaN, or when an operation of the kernel overflows: what is proved and what is not written yet there is in [What holds today](../getting-started/guarantees.md#overflow-and-non-finite-values).
- Anything about an operand that is not normalized, which only limbs given by the program can make: `from_limbs` in a build without checks, `from_limbs_unchecked`, or `limb[]` written directly.
